verdict: Avoid new aluminium exposure in Angul for now; lend only to downstream units with firm offtake and tight monthly monitoring, and decline commodity-price plays.
title: Angul aluminium & aluminium products: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Angul is a smelter-and-downstream town: primary metal from NALCO's complex feeds extruders, rolled-product and conductor units that convert ingots and billets into profiles, sheets and wire.** Cash is made on conversion margin, not on metal — the metal is a pass-through priced off the exchange, so the borrower earns a fixed spread per tonne and the metal price risk sits with whoever holds inventory. **Cost structure is power-heavy and working capital is metal-heavy:** power, alumina and labour are the fixed-ish costs, while receivables from OEMs and inventory of metal set the cash cycle. **So when a proposal lands, check the power tariff contract and the conversion spread per tonne first; if the spread is not documented, ask for the last four quarters' job-work invoices.**

## What has changed now
**The official data pack reads AVOID for this cluster [D], and the local demand signals are weak: Odisha GST collections grew +0.5% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D], and Odisha electricity demand +5.1% against India's +9.5% [D].** India-wide aluminium output (NIC 24) grew only +2.4% YoY [D], and Brent at $113/bbl [D] raises freight and power-linked costs across the chain. **The local news is promotional, not demand evidence:** Odisha is inviting downstream investors to the Angul Aluminium Park with assured raw material and incentives [1], and NALCO is tying up EGA's DX+ Ultra technology for a 0.5 MTPA smelter expansion [2] — both are supply-side and multi-year. **Peer results are strong but say nothing about Angul's small units:** Vedanta Aluminium's Q2FY27 revenue rose 41% to INR 22,066 crore with EBITDA of INR 10,192 crore at ~46% margin [3], profit more than doubled to INR 6,187 crore [5], and management guides net effective price in H2 about $50 lower than Q2 [4]. **That last line is the warning: the integrated producers are guiding prices down while Angul's converters buy metal at those prices.**

## Where the growth is
**Pursue downstream converters with firm OEM offtake — extruded profiles for construction and transport, and conductor/rod units selling to state utilities — because their revenue is conversion-linked and survives a metal price fall.** The Angul park pitch [1] means new units will seek term debt for plant and machinery; those are worth underwriting only with a committed buyer. **Avoid pure metal traders, scrap-based remelters with no offtake contract, and any unit whose margin depends on holding inventory through a price rise.** Rating evidence on a converter shows margins guided at 9.5–10% with healthy coverage [7], and another rated peer shows interest coverage of 10.99x and total debt to GCA of 0.85x as on March 31, 2026 [10] — use these as the shape of an acceptable downstream balance sheet, not as Angul benchmarks.

## How to grow safely
**Structure every new line as a working-capital facility against documented invoices, with the metal leg cash-margined or backed by a price hedge, and keep term debt to plant only.** Take monthly: stock-and-receivable statements, power bills, job-work invoices and the top-five buyer ledger. **Covenant a minimum conversion margin per tonne and a maximum inventory days; if inventory days cross the agreed level, ask for the buyer contract and reduce the drawing power.** Rating notes flag that margins stay sensitive to international aluminium prices and global logistics even with hedging [9], so price-linked covenants matter more than turnover covenants here.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the borrower's power bill and buyer concentration together — a converter losing one OEM account shows up in receivables before it shows in sales.** If Odisha GST growth stays below India's +6.1% [D] for another quarter, treat new-to-bank proposals in this cluster as unsecured until proven otherwise. **If a borrower's margin depends on the metal price holding, decline; the integrated peers themselves expect H2 realisations about $50 lower than Q2 [4].** Note that the rating sources [7][9][10] carry no clear dates and [8] is a generic methodology paper — treat them as directional only. **Sources say little specific about Angul's own unit-level finances; collect from customer before any sanction.**
